doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

chapter: New York studio and sideman work
title: 'Jazz ain't got no words'
summary: He recalls Sergeant Garr's remark and says jazz's message was never what a song was about.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Someone once said to you, “Jazz is okay but it ain’t got no words.”
Sergeant Garr in the Air Force, yeah, he said that to me. He’s right.
Well I don’t think I write jazz words, you know, I just write words.
But he’s right about jazz, I thought it was an interesting comment. It ain’t got no words.
It is a little leap that jazz has to take because it doesn’t have that immediate message of what’s the song about.
But that was never jazz’s message. If jazz had a message I don’t think it was talking about what the song was about. It’s just talking about look what we could do with this.
